title: Runs stop on silence, not total time; a stop reads hung, never failed
why: Fixed total-time limits break as code grows and turn slow passing runs into red refusals; the owner ruled they serve no outcome except ending hung runs.
note: Owner ruling 14:09 CST Nov 10, form confirmed 14:10 CST ("yes, that three-part form matches what I meant"), typed in the retrospective session, relayed by the coordinator 14:10 and 14:12 CST. (1) Stop on silence: a run ends only after it prints nothing for a while; a slow run that keeps printing is never cut. (2) A stop reads "stopped, no output for N min", never red and never a merge refusal; retry once, then report to the owner. (3) A total-time limit that must stay, such as CI's billing limit, is read from recent green runs each time, never stored as a number. Replaces merge/merge.py LINT_SECONDS 1200, lint/check_debt_retire.py TIMEOUT 600, hooks/mutate_guard.py and janitor/mutate_sweep.py 1200 each, lint/check_python_floor.py 300, and decision ci-job-caps' job limits. Open: the silence window N comes from measurement. Record: branch time-limits-end-hangs-only (new decision time-limits-end-hangs-only, ci-job-caps rewritten). Related: local-caps-interim-raise, capped-job-hides-red, retire-check-whole-suite. R3 holds this step (coordinator 11:22 CST Nov 12): merge.deadlineMinutes is a total-time limit too, read from recent green runs under part (3). Lane fixed-number-limits-census hands its ~25 time limits here. Lane picks 11:49 CST Nov 12 (reversible): scope, touched and impeccable-sync keep 5/10 min as named exceptions; window 30 green runs; the silence stop only reports until a local green run records a gap. A second hang: page item 557 hung-job-twice. Owner 11:51 CST Nov 12, item 557 a: a second hang turns all-jobs-passed red, labelled "hung"; the lane writes it into its decision.
